sanskrit_shloka:
मृत्कार्यं सकलं घटादि सततं मृन्मात्रमेवाहितं तद्वत्सज्जनितं सदात्मकमिदं सन्मात्रमेवाखिलम् ।
यस्मान्नास्ति सतः परं किमपि तत्सत्यं स आत्मा स्वयं तस्मात्तत्त्वमसि प्रशान्तममलं ब्रह्माद्वयं यत्परम् ॥ २५१ ॥
transliteration:
mṛtkāryaṃ sakalaṃ ghaṭādi satataṃ mṛnmātramevāhitaṃ tadvatsajjanitaṃ sadātmakamidaṃ sanmātramevākhilam |
yasmānnāsti sataḥ paraṃ kimapi tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā svayaṃ tasmāttattvamasi praśāntamamalaṃ brahmādvayaṃ yatparam || 251 ||
translation: All modifications of clay, such as the jar, which are always accepted by the mind as real, are (in reality) nothing but clay. Similarly, this entire universe which is produced from the real Brahman, is Brahman Itself and nothing but That. Because there is nothing else whatever but Brahman, and That is the only self-existent Reality, our very Self, therefore art thou that serene, pure, Supreme Brahman, the One without a second.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: All modifications of clay, such as the jar, which are always accepted by the mind as real, are (in reality) nothing but clay. Similarly, this entire universe which is produced from the real Brahman, is Brahman Itself and nothing but That. Because there is nothing else whatever but Brahman, and That is the only self-existent Reality, our very Self, therefore art thou that serene, pure, Supreme Brahman, the One without a second.

sanskrit_shloka:
निद्राकल्पितदेशकालविषयज्ञात्रादि सर्वं यथा मिथ्या तद्वदिहापि जाग्रति जगत्स्वाज्ञानकार्यत्वतः ।
यस्मादेवमिदं शरीरकरणप्राणाहमाद्यप्यसत् तस्मात्तत्त्वमसि प्रशान्तममलं ब्रह्माद्वयं यत्परम् ॥ २५२ ॥
transliteration:
nidrākalpitadeśakālaviṣayajñātrādi sarvaṃ yathā mithyā tadvadihāpi jāgrati jagatsvājñānakāryatvataḥ |
yasmādevamidaṃ śarīrakaraṇaprāṇāhamādyapyasat tasmāttattvamasi praśāntamamalaṃ brahmādvayaṃ yatparam || 252 ||
translation: As the place, time, objects, knower, etc., called up in dream are all unreal, so is also the world experienced here in the waking state, for it is all an effect of one’s own ignorance. Because this body, the organs, the Prāṇas, egoism, etc., are also thus unreal, therefore art thou that serene, pure, supreme Brahman, the One without a second.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: As the place, time, objects, knower, etc., called up in dream are all unreal, so is also the world experienced here in the waking state, for it is all an effect of one’s own ignorance. Because this body, the organs, the Prāṇas, egoism, etc., are also thus unreal, therefore art thou that serene, pure, supreme Brahman, the One without a second.

sanskrit_shloka:
यत्र भ्रान्त्या कल्पित तद्विवेके तत्तन्मात्रं नैव तस्माद्विभिन्नम् ।
स्वप्ने नष्टं स्वप्नविश्वं विचित्रं स्वस्माद्भिन्नं किन्नु दृष्टं प्रबोधे ॥ २५३ ॥
transliteration:
yatra bhrāntyā kalpita tadviveke tattanmātraṃ naiva tasmādvibhinnam |
svapne naṣṭaṃ svapnaviśvaṃ vicitraṃ svasmādbhinnaṃ kinnu dṛṣṭaṃ prabodhe || 253 ||
translation: (What is) erroneously supposed to exist in something, is, when the truth about it has been known, nothing but that substratum, and not at all different from it: The diversified dream universe (appears and) passes away in the dream itself. Does it appear on waking as something distinct from one’s own Self?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: (What is) erroneously supposed to exist in something, is, when the truth about it has been known, nothing but that substratum, and not at all different from it: The diversified dream universe (appears and) passes away in the dream itself. Does it appear on waking as something distinct from one’s own Self?

sanskrit_shloka:
जातिनीतिकुलगोत्रदूरगं नामरूपगुणदोषवर्जितम् ।
देशकालविषयातिवर्ति यद् ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५४ ॥
transliteration:
jātinītikulagotradūragaṃ nāmarūpaguṇadoṣavarjitam |
deśakālaviṣayātivarti yad brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 254 ||
translation: That which is beyond caste and creed, family and lineage; devoid of name and form, merit and demerit; transcending space, time and sense-object – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which is beyond caste and creed, family and lineage; devoid of name and form, merit and demerit; transcending space, time and sense-object – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
यत्परं सकलवागगोचरं गोचरं विमलबोधचक्षुषः ।
शुद्धचिद्घनमनादि वस्तु यद् ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५५ ॥
transliteration:
yatparaṃ sakalavāgagocaraṃ gocaraṃ vimalabodhacakṣuṣaḥ |
śuddhacidghanamanādi vastu yad brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 255 ||
translation: That Supreme Brahman which is beyond the range of all speech, but accessible to the eye of pure illumination; which is pure, the Embodiment of Knowledge, the beginningless entity – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That Supreme Brahman which is beyond the range of all speech, but accessible to the eye of pure illumination; which is pure, the Embodiment of Knowledge, the beginningless entity – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
षड्भिरूर्मिभिरयोगि योगिहृद् भावितं न करणैर्विभावितम् ।
बुद्ध्यवेद्यमनवद्यमस्ति यद् ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५६ ॥
transliteration:
ṣaḍbhirūrmibhirayogi yogihṛd bhāvitaṃ na karaṇairvibhāvitam |
buddhyavedyamanavadyamasti yad brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 256 ||
translation: That which is untouched by the sixfold wave; meditated upon by the Yogi’s heart, but not grasped by the sense-organs; which the Buddhi cannot know; and which is unimpeachable – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which is untouched by the sixfold wave; meditated upon by the Yogi’s heart, but not grasped by the sense-organs; which the Buddhi cannot know; and which is unimpeachable – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
भ्रान्तिकल्पितजगत्कलाश्रयं स्वाश्रयं च सदसद्विलक्षणम् ।
निष्कलं निरुपमानवद्धि यद् ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५७ ॥
transliteration:
bhrāntikalpitajagatkalāśrayaṃ svāśrayaṃ ca sadasadvilakṣaṇam |
niṣkalaṃ nirupamānavaddhi yad brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 257 ||
translation: That which is the substratum of the universe with its various subdivisions, which are all creations of delusion; which Itself has no other support; which is distinct from the gross and subtle; which has no parts, and has verily no exemplar – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which is the substratum of the universe with its various subdivisions, which are all creations of delusion; which Itself has no other support; which is distinct from the gross and subtle; which has no parts, and has verily no exemplar – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
जन्मवृद्धिपरिणत्यपक्षय व्याधिनाशनविहीनमव्ययम् ।
विश्वसृष्ट्यवविघातकारणं ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५८ ॥
transliteration:
janmavṛddhipariṇatyapakṣaya vyādhināśanavihīnamavyayam |
viśvasṛṣṭyavavighātakāraṇaṃ brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 258 ||
translation: That which is free from birth, growth, development, waste, disease and death; which is indestructible; which is the cause of the projection, maintenance and dissolution of the universe – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which is free from birth, growth, development, waste, disease and death; which is indestructible; which is the cause of the projection, maintenance and dissolution of the universe – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
अस्तभेदमनपास्तलक्षणं निस्तरङ्गजलराशिनिश्चलम् ।
नित्यमुक्तमविभक्तमूर्ति यद् ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५९ ॥
transliteration:
astabhedamanapāstalakṣaṇaṃ nistaraṅgajalarāśiniścalam |
nityamuktamavibhaktamūrti yad brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 259 ||
translation: That which is free from differentiation; whose essence is never non-existent; which is unmoved like the ocean without waves; the ever-free; of indivisible Form – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which is free from differentiation; whose essence is never non-existent; which is unmoved like the ocean without waves; the ever-free; of indivisible Form – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
एकमेव सदनेककारणं कारणान्तरनिरास्यकारणम् ।
कार्यकारणविलक्षणं स्वयं ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २६0 ॥
transliteration:
ekameva sadanekakāraṇaṃ kāraṇāntaranirāsyakāraṇam |
kāryakāraṇavilakṣaṇaṃ svayaṃ brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 260 ||
translation: That which, though One only, is the cause of the many; which refutes all other causes, but is Itself without cause; distinct from Māyā and its effect, the universe; and independent – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which, though One only, is the cause of the many; which refutes all other causes, but is Itself without cause; distinct from Māyā and its effect, the universe; and independent – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
निर्विकल्पकमनल्पमक्षरं यत्क्षराक्षरविलक्षणं परम् ।
नित्यमव्ययसुखं निरञ्जनं ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २६१ ॥
transliteration:
nirvikalpakamanalpamakṣaraṃ yatkṣarākṣaravilakṣaṇaṃ param |
nityamavyayasukhaṃ nirañjanaṃ brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 261 ||
translation: That which is free from duality; which is infinite and indestructible; distinct from the universe and Māyā, supreme, eternal; which is undying Bliss; taintless – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which is free from duality; which is infinite and indestructible; distinct from the universe and Māyā, supreme, eternal; which is undying Bliss; taintless – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
यद्विभाति सदनेकधा भ्रमान् नामरूपगुणविक्रियात्मना ।
हेमवत्स्वयमविक्रियं सदा ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २६२ ॥
transliteration:
yadvibhāti sadanekadhā bhramān nāmarūpaguṇavikriyātmanā |
hemavatsvayamavikriyaṃ sadā brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 262 ||
translation: That Reality which (though One) appears variously owing to delusion, taking on names and forms, attributes and changes, Itself always unchanged, like gold in its modifications – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That Reality which (though One) appears variously owing to delusion, taking on names and forms, attributes and changes, Itself always unchanged, like gold in its modifications – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
यच्चकास्त्यनपरं परात्परं प्रत्यगेकरसमात्मलक्षणम् ।
सत्यचित्सुखमनन्तमव्ययं ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २६३ ॥
transliteration:
yaccakāstyanaparaṃ parātparaṃ pratyagekarasamātmalakṣaṇam |
satyacitsukhamanantamavyayaṃ brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 263 ||
translation: That beyond which there is nothing; which shines even above Māyā, which again is superior to its effect, the universe; the inmost Self of all, free from differentiation; the Real Self, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute; infinite and immutable – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That beyond which there is nothing; which shines even above Māyā, which again is superior to its effect, the universe; the inmost Self of all, free from differentiation; the Real Self, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute; infinite and immutable – that Brahman art thou, meditate on this in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
उक्तमर्थमिममात्मनि स्वयं भावयेत्प्रथितयुक्तिभिर्धिया ।
संशयादिरहितं कराम्बुवत् तेन तत्त्वनिगमो भविष्यति ॥ २६४ ॥
transliteration:
uktamarthamimamātmani svayaṃ bhāvayetprathitayuktibhirdhiyā |
saṃśayādirahitaṃ karāmbuvat tena tattvanigamo bhaviṣyati || 264 ||
translation: On the Truth, inculcated above, one must oneself meditate in one’s mind, through the intellect, by means of the recognised arguments. By that means one will realise the truth free from doubt etc., like water in the palm of one’s hand.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: On the Truth, inculcated above, one must oneself meditate in one’s mind, through the intellect, by means of the recognised arguments. By that means one will realise the truth free from doubt etc., like water in the palm of one’s hand.

sanskrit_shloka:
संबोधमात्रं परिशुद्धतत्त्वं विज्ञाय सङ्घे नृपवच्च सैन्ये ।
तदाश्रयः स्वात्मनि सर्वदा स्थितो विलापय ब्रह्मणि विश्वजातम् ॥ २६५ ॥
transliteration:
saṃbodhamātraṃ pariśuddhatattvaṃ vijñāya saṅghe nṛpavacca sainye |
tadāśrayaḥ svātmani sarvadā sthito vilāpaya brahmaṇi viśvajātam || 265 ||
translation: Realising in this body the Knowledge Absolute free from Nescience and its effects – like the king in an army – and being ever established in thy own Self by resting on that Knowledge, merge the universe in Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Realising in this body the Knowledge Absolute free from Nescience and its effects – like the king in an army – and being ever established in thy own Self by resting on that Knowledge, merge the universe in Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
बुद्धौ गुहायां सदसद्विलक्षणं ब्रह्मास्ति सत्यं परमद्वितीयम् ।
तदात्मना योऽत्र वसेद्गुहायां पुनर्न तस्याङ्गगुहाप्रवेशः ॥ २६६ ॥
transliteration:
buddhau guhāyāṃ sadasadvilakṣaṇaṃ brahmāsti satyaṃ paramadvitīyam |
tadātmanā yo'tra vasedguhāyāṃ punarna tasyāṅgaguhāpraveśaḥ || 266 ||
translation: In the cave of the Buddhi there is the Brahman, distinct from the gross and subtle, the Existence Absolute, Supreme, the One without a second. For one who lives in this cave as Brahman, O beloved, there is no more entrance into the mother’s womb.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In the cave of the Buddhi there is the Brahman, distinct from the gross and subtle, the Existence Absolute, Supreme, the One without a second. For one who lives in this cave as Brahman, O beloved, there is no more entrance into the mother’s womb.

sanskrit_shloka:
ज्ञाते वस्तुन्यपि बलवती वासनानादिरेषा कर्ता भोक्ताप्यहमिति दृढा यास्य संसारहेतुः ।
प्रत्यग्दृष्ट्यात्मनि निवसता सापनेया प्रयत्नान् मुक्तिं प्राहुस्तदिह मुनयो वासनातानवं यत् ॥ २६७ ॥
transliteration:
jñāte vastunyapi balavatī vāsanānādireṣā kartā bhoktāpyahamiti dṛḍhā yāsya saṃsārahetuḥ |
pratyagdṛṣṭyātmani nivasatā sāpaneyā prayatnān muktiṃ prāhustadiha munayo vāsanātānavaṃ yat || 267 ||
translation: Even after the Truth has been realised, there remains that strong, beginningless, obstinate impression that one is the agent and experiencer, which is the cause of one’s transmigration. It has to be carefully removed by living in a state of constant identification with the Supreme Self. Sages call that Liberation which is the attenuation of Vāsanās (impressions) here and now.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Even after the Truth has been realised, there remains that strong, beginningless, obstinate impression that one is the agent and experiencer, which is the cause of one’s transmigration. It has to be carefully removed by living in a state of constant identification with the Supreme Self. Sages call that Liberation which is the attenuation of Vāsanās (impressions) here and now.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहं ममेति यो भावो देहाक्षादावनात्मनि ।
अध्यासोऽयं निरस्तव्यो विदुषा स्वात्मनिष्ठया ॥ २६८ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṃ mameti yo bhāvo dehākṣādāvanātmani |
adhyāso'yaṃ nirastavyo viduṣā svātmaniṣṭhayā || 268 ||
translation: The idea of 'me and mine' in the body, organs, etc., which are the non-Self – this superimposition the wise man must put a stop to, by identifying himself with the Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The idea of 'me and mine' in the body, organs, etc., which are the non-Self – this superimposition the wise man must put a stop to, by identifying himself with the Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
ज्ञात्वा स्वं प्रत्यगात्मानं बुद्धितद्वृत्तिसाक्षिणम् ।
सोऽहमित्येव सद्वृत्त्यानात्मन्यात्ममतिं जहि ॥ २६९ ॥
transliteration:
jñātvā svaṃ pratyagātmānaṃ buddhitadvṛttisākṣiṇam |
so'hamityeva sadvṛttyānātmanyātmamatiṃ jahi || 269 ||
translation: Realising thy own Inmost Self, the Witness of the Buddhi and its modifications, and constantly revolving the positive thought, 'I am That', conquer this identification with the non-Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Realising thy own Inmost Self, the Witness of the Buddhi and its modifications, and constantly revolving the positive thought, 'I am That', conquer this identification with the non-Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
लोकानुवर्तनं त्यक्त्वा त्यक्त्वा देहानुवर्तनम् ।
शास्त्रानुवर्तनं त्यक्त्वा स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २७0 ॥
transliteration:
lokānuvartanaṃ tyaktvā tyaktvā dehānuvartanam |
śāstrānuvartanaṃ tyaktvā svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 270 ||
translation: Relinquishing the observance of social formalities, giving up all ideas of trimming up the body, and avoiding too mush engrossment with the Scriptures, do away with the superimposition that has come upon thyself.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Relinquishing the observance of social formalities, giving up all ideas of trimming up the body, and avoiding too mush engrossment with the Scriptures, do away with the superimposition that has come upon thyself.

sanskrit_shloka:
लोकवासनया जन्तोः शास्त्रवासनयापि च ।
देहवासनया ज्ञानं यथावन्नैव जायते ॥ २७१ ॥
transliteration:
lokavāsanayā jantoḥ śāstravāsanayāpi ca |
dehavāsanayā jñānaṃ yathāvannaiva jāyate || 271 ||
translation: Owing to the desire to run after society, the passion for too much study of the Scriptures and the desire to keep the body in good trim, people cannot attain to proper Realisation.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Owing to the desire to run after society, the passion for too much study of the Scriptures and the desire to keep the body in good trim, people cannot attain to proper Realisation.

sanskrit_shloka:
संसारकारागृहमोक्षमिच्छोर् अयोमायां पादनिबन्धशृङ्खलम् ।
वदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः पटु वासनात्रयं योऽस्माद्विमुक्तः समुपैति मुक्तिम् ॥ २७२ ॥
transliteration:
saṃsārakārāgṛhamokṣamicchor ayoMāyāṃ pādanibandhaśṛṅkhalam |
vadanti tajjñāḥ paṭu vāsanātrayaṃ yo'smādvimuktaḥ samupaiti muktim || 272 ||
translation: For one who seeks deliverance from the prison of this world (Samsara), those three desires have been designated by the wise as strong iron fetters to shackle one’s feet. He who is free from them truly attains to Liberation.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: For one who seeks deliverance from the prison of this world (Samsara), those three desires have been designated by the wise as strong iron fetters to shackle one’s feet. He who is free from them truly attains to Liberation.

sanskrit_shloka:
जलादिसंसर्गवशात्प्रभूत दुर्गन्धधूतागरुदिव्यवासना ।
संघर्षणेनैव विभाति सम्यग् विधूयमाने सति बाह्यगन्धे ॥ २७३ ॥
transliteration:
jalādisaṃsargavaśātprabhūta durgandhadhūtāgarudivyavāsanā |
saṃgharṣaṇenaiva vibhāti samyag vidhūyamāne sati bāhyagandhe || 273 ||
translation: The lovely odour of the Agaru (agalochum) which is hidden by a powerful stench due to its contact with water etc., manifests itself as soon as the foreign smell has been fully removed by rubbing.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The lovely odour of the Agaru (agalochum) which is hidden by a powerful stench due to its contact with water etc., manifests itself as soon as the foreign smell has been fully removed by rubbing.

sanskrit_shloka:
अन्तःश्रितानन्तदूरन्तवासना धूलीविलिप्ता परमात्मवासना ।
प्रज्ञातिसंघर्षणतो विशुद्धा प्रतीयते चन्दनगन्धवत्स्फुटम् ॥ २७४ ॥
transliteration:
antaḥśritānantadūrantavāsanā dhūlīviliptā paramātmavāsanā |
prajñātisaṃgharṣaṇato viśuddhā pratīyate candanagandhavatsphuṭam || 274 ||
translation: Like the fragrance of the sandal-wood, the perfume of the Supreme Self, which is covered with the dust of endless, violent impressions imbedded in the mind, when purified by the constant friction of Knowledge, is (again) clearly perceived.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Like the fragrance of the sandal-wood, the perfume of the Supreme Self, which is covered with the dust of endless, violent impressions imbedded in the mind, when purified by the constant friction of Knowledge, is (again) clearly perceived.

sanskrit_shloka:
अनात्मवासनाजालैस्तिरोभूतात्मवासना ।
नित्यात्मनिष्ठया तेषां नाशे भाति स्वयं स्फुटम् ॥ २७५ ॥
transliteration:
anātmavāsanājālaistirobhūtātmavāsanā |
nityātmaniṣṭhayā teṣāṃ nāśe bhāti svayaṃ sphuṭam || 275 ||
translation: The desire for Self-realisation is obscured by innumerable desires for things other than the Self. When they have been destroyed by the constant attachment to the Self, the Ātman clearly manifests Itself of Its own accord.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The desire for Self-realisation is obscured by innumerable desires for things other than the Self. When they have been destroyed by the constant attachment to the Self, the Ātman clearly manifests Itself of Its own accord.

sanskrit_shloka:
यथा यथा प्रत्यगवस्थितं मनः तथा तथा मुञ्चति बाह्यवासनाम् ।
निःशेषमोक्षे सति वासनानां आत्मानुभूतिः प्रतिबन्धशून्या ॥ २७६ ॥
transliteration:
yathā yathā pratyagavasthitaṃ manaḥ tathā tathā muñcati bāhyavāsanām |
niḥśeṣamokṣe sati vāsanānāṃ ātmānubhūtiḥ pratibandhaśūnyā || 276 ||
translation: As the mind becomes gradually established in the Inmost Self, it proportionately gives up the desires for external objects. And when all such desires have been eliminated, there takes place the unobstructed realisation of the Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: As the mind becomes gradually established in the Inmost Self, it proportionately gives up the desires for external objects. And when all such desires have been eliminated, there takes place the unobstructed realisation of the Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वात्मन्येव सदा स्थित्वा मनो नश्यति योगिनः ।
वासनानां क्षयश्चातः स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २७७ ॥
transliteration:
svātmanyeva sadā sthitvā mano naśyati yoginaḥ |
vāsanānāṃ kṣayaścātaḥ svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 277 ||
translation: The Yogi’s mind dies, being constantly fixed on his own Self. Thence follows the cessation of desires. Therefore do away with thy superimposition.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Yogi’s mind dies, being constantly fixed on his own Self. Thence follows the cessation of desires. Therefore do away with thy superimposition.

sanskrit_shloka:
तमो द्वाभ्यां रजः सत्त्वात्सत्त्वं शुद्धेन नश्यति ।
तस्मात्सत्त्वमवष्टभ्य स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २७८ ॥
transliteration:
tamo dvābhyāṃ rajaḥ sattvātsattvaṃ śuddhena naśyati |
tasmātsattvamavaṣṭabhya svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 278 ||
translation: Tamas is destroyed by both Sattva and Rajas, Rajas by Sattva, and Sattva dies when purified. Therefore do way with thy superimposition through the help of Sattva.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Tamas is destroyed by both Sattva and Rajas, Rajas by Sattva, and Sattva dies when purified. Therefore do way with thy superimposition through the help of Sattva.

sanskrit_shloka:
प्रारब्धं पुष्यति वपुरिति निश्चित्य निश्चलः ।
धैर्यमालम्ब्य यत्नेन स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २७९ ॥
transliteration:
prārabdhaṃ puṣyati vapuriti niścitya niścalaḥ |
dhairyamālambya yatnena svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 279 ||
translation: Knowing for certain that the Prārabdha work will maintain this body, remain quiet and do away with thy superimposition carefully and with patience.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Knowing for certain that the Prārabdha work will maintain this body, remain quiet and do away with thy superimposition carefully and with patience.

sanskrit_shloka:
नाहं जीवः परं ब्रह्मेत्यतद्व्यावृत्तिपूर्वकम् ।
वासनावेगतः प्राप्तस्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८0 ॥
transliteration:
nāhaṃ jīvaḥ paraṃ brahmetyatadvyāvṛttipūrvakam |
vāsanāvegataḥ prāptasvādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 280 ||
translation: 'I am not the individual soul, but the Supreme Brahman' – eliminating thus all that is not-Self, do away with thy superimposition, which has come through the momentum of (past) impressions.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: 'I am not the individual soul, but the Supreme Brahman' – eliminating thus all that is not-Self, do away with thy superimposition, which has come through the momentum of (past) impressions.

sanskrit_shloka:
श्रुत्या युक्त्या स्वानुभूत्या ज्ञात्वा सार्वात्म्यमात्मनः ।
क्वचिदाभासतः प्राप्तस्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८१ ॥
transliteration:
śrutyā yuktyā svānubhūtyā jñātvā sārvātmyamātmanaḥ |
kvacidābhāsataḥ prāptasvādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 281 ||
translation: Realising thyself as the Self of all by means of Scripture, reasoning and by thy own realisation, do away thy superimposition, even when a trace of it seems to appear.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Realising thyself as the Self of all by means of Scripture, reasoning and by thy own realisation, do away thy superimposition, even when a trace of it seems to appear.

sanskrit_shloka:
अनादानविसर्गाभ्यामीषन्नास्ति क्रिया मुनेः ।
तदेकनिष्ठया नित्यं स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८२ ॥
transliteration:
anādānavisargābhyāmīṣannāsti kriyā muneḥ |
tadekaniṣṭhayā nityaṃ svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 282 ||
translation: The sage has no connection with action, since he has no idea of accepting or giving up. Therefore, through constant engrossment on the Brahman, do away with thy superimposition.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The sage has no connection with action, since he has no idea of accepting or giving up. Therefore, through constant engrossment on the Brahman, do away with thy superimposition.

sanskrit_shloka:
तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्योत्थब्रह्मात्मैकत्वबोधतः ।
ब्रह्मण्यात्मत्वदार्ढ्याय स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८३ ॥
transliteration:
tattvamasyādivākyotthabrahmātmaikatvabodhataḥ |
brahmaṇyātmatvadārḍhyāya svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 283 ||
translation: Through the realisation of the identity of Brahman and the soul, resulting from such great dicta as 'Thou art That', do away with thy superimposition, with a view to strengthening thy identification with Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Through the realisation of the identity of Brahman and the soul, resulting from such great dicta as 'Thou art That', do away with thy superimposition, with a view to strengthening thy identification with Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहंभावस्य देहेऽस्मिन्निःशेषविलयावधि ।
सावधानेन युक्तात्मा स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८४ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṃbhāvasya dehe'sminniḥśeṣavilayāvadhi |
sāvadhānena yuktātmā svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 284 ||
translation: Until the identification with this body is completely rooted out, do away with thy superimposition with watchfulness and a concentrated mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Until the identification with this body is completely rooted out, do away with thy superimposition with watchfulness and a concentrated mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
प्रतीतिर्जीवजगतोः स्वप्नवद्भाति यावता ।
तावन्निरन्तरं विद्वन्स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८५ ॥
transliteration:
pratītirjīvajagatoḥ svapnavadbhāti yāvatā |
tāvannirantaraṃ vidvansvādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 285 ||
translation: So long as even a dream-like perception of the universe and souls persists, do away with thy superimposition, O learned man, without the least break.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: So long as even a dream-like perception of the universe and souls persists, do away with thy superimposition, O learned man, without the least break.

sanskrit_shloka:
निद्राया लोकवार्तायाः शब्दादेरपि विस्मृतेः ।
क्वचिन्नावसरं दत्त्वा चिन्तयात्मानमात्मनि ॥ २८६ ॥
transliteration:
nidrāyā lokavārtāyāḥ śabdāderapi vismṛteḥ |
kvacinnāvasaraṃ dattvā cintayātmānamātmani || 286 ||
translation: Without giving the slightest chance to oblivion on account of sleep, concern in secular matters or the sense-objects, reflect on the Self in thy mind.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Without giving the slightest chance to oblivion on account of sleep, concern in secular matters or the sense-objects, reflect on the Self in thy mind.

sanskrit_shloka:
मातापित्रोर्मलोद्भूतं मलमांसमायां वपुः ।
त्यक्त्वा चाण्डालवद्दूरं ब्रह्मीभूय कृती भव ॥ २८७ ॥
transliteration:
mātāpitrormalodbhūtaṃ malamāṃsaMāyāṃ vapuḥ |
tyaktvā cāṇḍālavaddūraṃ brahmībhūya kṛtī bhava || 287 ||
translation: Shunning from a safe distance the body which has come from impurities of the parents and itself consists of flesh and impurities – as one does an outcast – be thou Brahman and realise the consummation of thy life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Shunning from a safe distance the body which has come from impurities of the parents and itself consists of flesh and impurities – as one does an outcast – be thou Brahman and realise the consummation of thy life.

sanskrit_shloka:
घटाकाशं महाकाश इवात्मानं परात्मनि ।
विलाप्याखण्डभावेन तूष्णी भव सदा मुने ॥ २८८ ॥
transliteration:
ghaṭākāśaṃ mahākāśa ivātmānaṃ parātmani |
vilāpyākhaṇḍabhāvena tūṣṇī bhava sadā mune || 288 ||
translation: Merging the finite soul in the Supreme Self, like the space enclosed by a jar in the infinite space, by means of meditation on their identity, always keep quiet, O sage.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Merging the finite soul in the Supreme Self, like the space enclosed by a jar in the infinite space, by means of meditation on their identity, always keep quiet, O sage.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वप्रकाशमधिष्ठानं स्वयंभूय सदात्मना ।
ब्रह्माण्डमपि पिण्डाण्डं त्यज्यतां मलभाण्डवत् ॥ २८९ ॥
transliteration:
svaprakāśamadhiṣṭhānaṃ svayaṃbhūya sadātmanā |
brahmāṇḍamapi piṇḍāṇḍaṃ tyajyatāṃ malabhāṇḍavat || 289 ||
translation: Becoming thyself the self-effulgent Brahman, the substratum of all phenomena – as that Reality give up both the macrocosm and the microcosm, like two filthy receptacles.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Becoming thyself the self-effulgent Brahman, the substratum of all phenomena – as that Reality give up both the macrocosm and the microcosm, like two filthy receptacles.

sanskrit_shloka:
चिदात्मनि सदानन्दे देहारूढामहंधियम् ।
निवेश्य लिङ्गमुत्सृज्य केवलो भव सर्वदा ॥ २९0 ॥
transliteration:
cidātmani sadānande dehārūḍhāmahaṃdhiyam |
niveśya liṅgamutsṛjya kevalo bhava sarvadā || 290 ||
translation: Transferring the identification now rooted in the body to the Ātman, the Existence- Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, and discarding the subtle body, be thou ever alone, independent.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Transferring the identification now rooted in the body to the Ātman, the Existence- Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, and discarding the subtle body, be thou ever alone, independent.

sanskrit_shloka:
यत्रैष जगदाभासो दर्पणान्तः पुरं यथा ।
तद्ब्रह्माहमिति ज्ञात्वा कृतकृत्यो भविष्यसि ॥ २९१ ॥
transliteration:
yatraiṣa jagadābhāso darpaṇāntaḥ puraṃ yathā |
tadbrahmāhamiti jñātvā kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi || 291 ||
translation: That in which there is this reflection of the universe, as of a city in a mirror – that Brahman art thou; knowing this thou wilt attain the consummation of thy life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That in which there is this reflection of the universe, as of a city in a mirror – that Brahman art thou; knowing this thou wilt attain the consummation of thy life.

sanskrit_shloka:
यत्सत्यभूतं निजरूपमाद्यं चिदद्वयानन्दमरूपमक्रियम् ।
तदेत्य मिथ्यावपुरुत्सृजेत शैलूषवद्वेषमुपात्तमात्मनः ॥ २९२ ॥
transliteration:
yatsatyabhūtaṃ nijarūpamādyaṃ cidadvayānandamarūpamakriyam |
tadetya mithyāvapurutsṛjeta śailūṣavadveṣamupāttamātmanaḥ || 292 ||
translation: That which is real and one’s own primeval Essence, that Knowledge and Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, which is beyond form and activity – attaining That one should cease to identify oneself with one’s false bodies, like an actor giving up his assumed mask.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which is real and one’s own primeval Essence, that Knowledge and Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, which is beyond form and activity – attaining That one should cease to identify oneself with one’s false bodies, like an actor giving up his assumed mask.

sanskrit_shloka:
सर्वात्मना दृश्यमिदं मृषैव नैवाहमर्थः क्षणिकत्वदर्शनात् ।
जानाम्यहं सर्वमिति प्रतीतिः कुतोऽहमादेः क्षणिकस्य सिध्येत् ॥ २९३ ॥
transliteration:
sarvātmanā dṛśyamidaṃ mṛṣaiva naivāhamarthaḥ kṣaṇikatvadarśanāt |
jānāmyahaṃ sarvamiti pratītiḥ kuto'hamādeḥ kṣaṇikasya sidhyet || 293 ||
translation: This objective universe is absolutely unreal; neither is egoism a reality, for it is observed to be momentary. How can the perception, 'I know all', be true of egoism etc., which are momentary?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: This objective universe is absolutely unreal; neither is egoism a reality, for it is observed to be momentary. How can the perception, 'I know all', be true of egoism etc., which are momentary?

sanskrit_shloka:
अहंपदार्थस्त्वहमादिसाक्षी नित्यं सुषुप्तावपि भावदर्शनात् ।
ब्रूते ह्यजो नित्य इति श्रुतिः स्वयं तत्प्रत्यगात्मा सदसद्विलक्षणः ॥ २९४ ॥
transliteration:
ahaṃpadārthastvahamādisākṣī nityaṃ suṣuptāvapi bhāvadarśanāt |
brūte hyajo nitya iti śrutiḥ svayaṃ tatpratyagātmā sadasadvilakṣaṇaḥ || 294 ||
translation: But the real ‘I' is that which witnesses the ego and the rest. It exists always, even in the state of profound sleep. The Shruti itself says, 'It is birthless, eternal', etc. Therefore the Paramātman is different from the gross and subtle bodies.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: But the real ‘I' is that which witnesses the ego and the rest. It exists always, even in the state of profound sleep. The Shruti itself says, 'It is birthless, eternal', etc. Therefore the Paramātman is different from the gross and subtle bodies.

sanskrit_shloka:
विकारिणां सर्वविकारवेत्ता नित्याविकारो भवितुं समर्हति ।
मनोरथस्वप्नसुषुप्तिषु स्फुटं पुनः पुनर्दृष्टमसत्त्वमेतयोः ॥ २९५ ॥
transliteration:
vikāriṇāṃ sarvavikāravettā nityāvikāro bhavituṃ samarhati |
manorathasvapnasuṣuptiṣu sphuṭaṃ punaḥ punardṛṣṭamasattvametayoḥ || 295 ||
translation: The knower of all changes in things subject to change should necessarily be eternal and changeless. The unreality of the gross and subtle bodies is again and again clearly observed in imagination, dream and profound sleep.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The knower of all changes in things subject to change should necessarily be eternal and changeless. The unreality of the gross and subtle bodies is again and again clearly observed in imagination, dream and profound sleep.

sanskrit_shloka:
अतोऽभिमानं त्यज मांसपिण्डे पिण्डाभिमानिन्यपि बुद्धिकल्पिते ।
कालत्रयाबाध्यमखण्डबोधं ज्ञात्वा स्वमात्मानमुपैहि शान्तिम् ॥ २९६ ॥
transliteration:
ato'bhimānaṃ tyaja māṃsapiṇḍe piṇḍābhimāninyapi buddhikalpite |
kālatrayābādhyamakhaṇḍabodhaṃ jñātvā svamātmānamupaihi śāntim || 296 ||
translation: Therefore give up the identification with this lump of flesh, the gross body, as well as with the ego or the subtle body, which are both imagined by the Buddhi. Realising thy own Self, which is Knowledge Absolute and not to be denied in the past, present or future, attain to Peace.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Therefore give up the identification with this lump of flesh, the gross body, as well as with the ego or the subtle body, which are both imagined by the Buddhi. Realising thy own Self, which is Knowledge Absolute and not to be denied in the past, present or future, attain to Peace.

sanskrit_shloka:
त्यजाभिमानं कुलगोत्रनाम रूपाश्रमेष्वार्द्रशवाश्रितेषु ।
लिङ्गस्य धर्मानपि कर्तृतादिंस् त्यक्ता भवाखण्डसुखस्वरूपः ॥ २९७ ॥
transliteration:
tyajābhimānaṃ kulagotranāma rūpāśrameṣvārdraśavāśriteṣu |
liṅgasya dharmānapi kartṛtādiṃs tyaktā bhavākhaṇḍasukhasvarūpaḥ || 297 ||
translation: Cease to identify thyself with the family, lineage, name, form and the order of life, which pertain to the body that is like a rotten corpse (to a man of realisation). Similarly, giving up ideas of agency and so forth, which are attributes of the subtle body, be the Essence of Bliss Absolute.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Cease to identify thyself with the family, lineage, name, form and the order of life, which pertain to the body that is like a rotten corpse (to a man of realisation). Similarly, giving up ideas of agency and so forth, which are attributes of the subtle body, be the Essence of Bliss Absolute.

sanskrit_shloka:
सन्त्यन्ये प्रतिबन्धाः पुंसः संसारहेतवो दृष्टाः ।
तेषामेवं मूलं प्रथमविकारो भवत्यहंकारः ॥ २९८ ॥
transliteration:
santyanye pratibandhāḥ puṃsaḥ saṃsārahetavo dṛṣṭāḥ |
teṣāmevaṃ mūlaṃ prathamavikāro bhavatyahaṃkāraḥ || 298 ||
translation: Other obstacles are also observed to exist for men, which lead to transmigration. The root of them, for the above reasons, is the first modification of Nescience called egoism.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Other obstacles are also observed to exist for men, which lead to transmigration. The root of them, for the above reasons, is the first modification of Nescience called egoism.

sanskrit_shloka:
यावत्स्यात्स्वस्य संबन्धोऽहंकारेण दुरात्मना ।
तावन्न लेशमात्रापि मुक्तिवार्ता विलक्षणा ॥ २९९ ॥
transliteration:
yāvatsyātsvasya saṃbandho'haṃkāreṇa durātmanā |
tāvanna leśamātrāpi muktivārtā vilakṣaṇā || 299 ||
translation: So long as one has any relation to this wicked ego, there should not be the least talk about Liberation, which is unique.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: So long as one has any relation to this wicked ego, there should not be the least talk about Liberation, which is unique.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहंकारग्रहान्मुक्तः स्वरूपमुपपद्यते ।
चन्द्रवद्विमलः पूर्णः सदानन्दः स्वयंप्रभः ॥ ३00 ॥
transliteration:
ahaṃkāragrahānmuktaḥ svarūpamupapadyate |
candravadvimalaḥ pūrṇaḥ sadānandaḥ svayaṃprabhaḥ || 300 ||
translation: Freed from the clutches of egoism, as the moon from those of Rāhu, man attains to his real nature, and becomes pure, infinite, ever blissful and self-luminous.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Freed from the clutches of egoism, as the moon from those of Rāhu, man attains to his real nature, and becomes pure, infinite, ever blissful and self-luminous.
